item.title: FreeBSD exec_args_adjust_args() Out-of-Bounds memmove — Local Privilege Escalation via sshd Race (CVE-2026-7270)
item.description:
Metadata

Field Value
Date Added 2026-07-05
Last Updated 2026-06
Author / Researcher babyshen (mirrored from califio/publications MADBugs writeup)
CVE / Advisory CVE-2026-7270
Category binary
Severity Critical
CVSS Score Not specified in source
Status Weaponized
Tags freebsd, kernel, lpe, memmove, oob, race-condition, ld_preload, sshd, cwe-190, cwe-787
Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System FreeBSD kernel — sys/kern/kern_exec.c exec_args_adjust_args()
Versions Affected FreeBSD 11.0 through 14.4 (all releases at time of disclosure)
Language / Platform C exploit + QEMU automation script
Authentication Required Local unprivileged shell
Network Access Required No (local exploit; targets local sshd via loopback race)

Summary

An operator-precedence bug in FreeBSD’s exec_args_adjust_args() (present since 2013) computes a memmove size using + consume instead of - consume, causing the copy length to be roughly double the correct value. With a ~265KB argv[0] supplied via a shebang exec, the resulting memmove overflows the exec_map entry by ~2KB into an adjacent entry with no crash or fault. By racing this overflow against sshd’s fork/execv on incoming connections, the exploit plants an LD_PRELOAD reference in sshd-session’s exec_map entry; since sshd-session runs root-to-root with no suid/sgid transition, the runtime linker honors LD_PRELOAD, and the attacker’s shared object constructor executes as uid 0, dropping a setuid-root shell.

item.title: OpenSSH regreSSHion Signal-Handler Race Unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2024-6387)
item.description:
Metadata

Author / Researcher Qualys Threat Research Unit (disclosure); 7etsuo (public PoC implementation)
CVE / Advisory CVE-2024-6387
Category network
Severity High
CVSS Score 8.1 (CVSSv3)
Status Weaponized
Tags RCE, OpenSSH, sshd, glibc, race-condition, SIGALRM, unauthenticated
Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System OpenSSH server daemon (sshd) on glibc-based Linux
Versions Affected OpenSSH 8.5p1 through 9.7p1 on glibc-based Linux distributions (fixed in 9.8p1)
Language / Platform C / Linux (glibc)
Authentication Required No
Network Access Required Yes

Summary

CVE-2024-6387 (regreSSHion) is a signal-handler race condition in OpenSSH sshd that reintroduced a previously fixed bug class and can allow unauthenticated remote code execution as root on glibc-based Linux systems. The issue is triggered around LoginGraceTime signal handling where async-signal-unsafe behavior is reachable during authentication timeout processing. Public PoC code was released shortly after disclosure, and broad internet scanning/exploitation activity has been reported, including inclusion in CISA KEV.
